To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two-nucleon correlations and light cluster production are affected by the momentum-dependent nuclear potential, leading, respectively, to a reduced and enhanced sensitivity of their observables to nuclear symmetry energy.

the effects due to momentum dependence of nuclear potentials on two-nucleons correlation functions and light clusters productions are not negligible, and the t/$^{4}$He ratio can still be used to constrain the density dependence of isospin asymmetric nuclear matter.

both observables of the two-nucleon momentum correlation function and the light cluster production are affected by the momentum dependence in the nuclear potential, and thus their sensitivity to the symmetry energy becomes weaker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects due to nuclear potential on light cluster production and two-nucleon correlations in heavy-ion collisions.
the study of nuclear matter properties by using the two-nucleon correlations and light cluster production.
the effects due to nuclear momentum-dependent potential on the correlation functions and light-cluster production in heavy-ion collisions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the momentum dependence of the nuclear potential plays a significant role in the study of nuclear equation of state, but the effects due to momentum dependence can be canceled to some extent by a proper choice of observable.
the momentum dependence of the nuclear potential should be included in the transport model calculation for a reliable extraction of nuclear symmetry energy from heavy-ion collisions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the momentum dependence of symmetry potential is crucial for a proper interpretation of experimental data on light cluster production in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energy.

the momentum dependence of the isoscalar potential plays a crucial role in the determination of the nuclear equation of state from the two-nucleon correlations as well as light cluster production in heavy-ion collisions.
